title: Optical Trapping of Plasmonic Nanoparticles for In Situ Surface-Enhanced Raman Spectroscopy Characterizations
protocol: Direct a 532 nm laser beam into the flex port of the optical tweezer microscope.
Align the 532 nm laser beam with a 750 nm long-pass dichroic mirror in the stereo double-layer pathways.
Combine the aligned laser beam with the original trapping laser beams to focus on the sample chamber.
Collect backscattered light from the sample chamber using another 750 nm long-pass dichroic mirror.
Redirect collected light into a spectrometer containing a liquid-nitrogen-cooled CCD camera.
Place a 532 nm notch filter in front of the entrance slit of the spectrometer before acquisition.
Heat 50 mL of 1 mM AgNO3 aqueous solution to boiling in a round-bottomed flask.
Add 1.0 mL of 0.1 M trisodium citrate dropwise into the boiled AgNO3 aqueous solution.
Keep the mixture boiling for 16 min under constant stirring.
Cool the mixture to room temperature and observe yellowish coloration.
Centrifuge the AgNP colloids at 2000 × g for 5 min at room temperature.
Remove the supernatant using a pipette.
Resuspend the AgNP colloids with 1 mL of de-ionized water (resistivity of 18.2 MΩ cm).
Repeat steps 2.5 and 2.6 thrice to remove residual reducing agent.
Characterize the size distribution of AgNPs using scanning electron microscopy.
Confirm the uniformity of AgNPs using dynamic light scattering.
Estimate the AgNP concentration as 0.1 nM by UV absorbance.
Add 200 µL of 2 mM DSNB to 1 mL of AgNP colloid.
Incubate at room temperature for 3 h to coat a layer of DSNB on the surface of AgNPs.
Centrifuge the AgNP-DSNB mixture at 2,000 × g for 5 min at room temperature.
Remove the supernatant.
Resuspend the AgNP-DSNB with 1 mL of de-ionized water.
Repeat steps to remove excess DSNB.
Record UV-visible spectra of the AgNP colloid and AgNP-DSNB solution.
Attach the frame tape to the glass slide.
Create a chamber with dimensions 1.0 cm length × 1.0 cm width × 0.25 mm height.
Add approximately 25 μL of AgNP-DSNB solution into the frame.
Place a coverslip on top of the frame tape and seal it.
Fill a container with liquid nitrogen to cool the CCD camera to -120 °C.
Block the Raman probe beam path using a magnetic laser safety screen.
Turn on the 532 nm Raman excitation source laser.
Fix the sample chamber containing AgNP-DSNB solution onto the chamber holder.
Add water to the water-immersed objective (60x magnification, numerical aperture of 1.2).
Place the chamber holder above the objective on the microstage.
Apply immersion oil on top of the coverslip.
Position the oil-immersed condenser to visualize particles on the microscope camera.
Adjust the Z position of the objective using the knob until a white spot appears on the microscope camera, indicating focus on the bottom glass surface of the chamber.
Adjust the X- and Y-positions of the microstage to move the chamber so that the central region is at the white spot.
Open the optical tweezer control software and use the joystick control to align the 1064 nm trapping laser with the white spot.
Tune the microscope's Z position knob to move the objective upward until the white spot disappears from the camera image.
Turn on the 1064 nm trapping laser to attract AgNPs in the chamber and create a plasmonic AgNP assembly.
Adjust the trapping laser beam intensity as needed to avoid overheating or bubble formation.
Increase the trapping laser power and irradiation time if no AgNP assembly is formed.
Adjust the position of the sample microstage to place the dark spot of the plasmonic AgNP assembly under the focus of the 532 nm Raman probe beam for spectroscopic measurements.
Place ND filters in front of the 532 nm Raman laser outlet.
Adjust the power output to 10 mW.
Input an acquisition time of 10 s into the spectrum software settings panel.
Click on the Acquire button to start spectral acquisition.
